correctness.rationale: The repaired final claim is the sharp order-n envelope, not an original claim to the general connected-subtree norm. For every active forest F of the symmetric slope constraints, strict-KKT data realize an open projection cell with derivative equal to its connected-component averaging operator Q_F. A tree cut-indicator basis gives the already published local norm (b b_A+a b_B)/(a+b). If the component S has s vertices, b_A+b_B<=n-s and a,b<=s-1, so every such gain is bounded by (s-1)(n-s)/s. The n-vertex broom made of an s-vertex path plus n-s leaves at one endpoint achieves equality on the cut at its first edge, and the strict cell yields an actual finite input pair. Thus M_n=max(1,max_{2<=s<=n-1}(s-1)(n-s)/s). The discrete difference n/[s(s+1)]-1 determines the first s with s(s+1)>=n, including possible integer ties; f_n(s)=n+1-s-n/s and exact deficit (s-sqrt n)^2/s show M_n=n+1-2sqrt n+O(n^-1/2). Independently checked exact cases through n=29; the proof is all n.
